1.word_for_word: चतुष्पञ्चाशत्तमे तु जित्वा राज्ञोऽरिपक्षगान् — In the fifty-fourth year he defeated the king's enemies; रुक्मिणं च विरुप्याथ भैष्म्याः पाणिं पुरेऽग्रहीत् — Then he disturbed Rukmi and took Bhaishma's hand in the city; इतीति "अहो धिग् अस्मान्" इत्य् एवं वदन्तः । — They said, "Oh, woe to us.; सुसंरब्धाः क्रोधाविष्टाः । — They were well-enraged and furious.; दंशिताः कृत-सन्नाहाः । — They were bitten and made-up.; परिक्रान्ताः परिवृताः । — They’ve been surrounded and surrounded.; अन्वीयुर् अन्वधावन् ॥१॥ — They followed him and ran after him.
1.translation: In the fifty-fourth year he defeated the king's enemies Then he disturbed Rukmi and took Bhaishma's hand in the city They said, "Oh, woe to us. They were well-enraged and furious. They were bitten and made-up. They’ve been surrounded and surrounded. They followed him and ran after him.

3.word_for_word: परेषां शराणां बाहुल्ये यादवानामचलत्वे दृष्टान्तः । — This is an illustration of the unsteadiness of the Yadavas in the multitude of arrows fired by others; मेघा इति ॥३॥ — Megha iti ॥3॥
3.translation: This is an illustration of the unsteadiness of the Yadavas in the multitude of arrows fired by others Megha iti ॥3॥

5.word_for_word: मा स्म भैः मा भयं कुरु । — Don’t be afraid, don’t be afraid.; हे वामलोचने वाराक्षि । — O left-eyed Varakshi.; तावकैस्त्वदीयैः कृत्वा ॥५॥ — Having done it with your servants.
5.translation: Don’t be afraid, don’t be afraid. O left-eyed Varakshi. Having done it with your servants.

6.word_for_word: स चासौ विक्रमश् च तम् ॥६॥ — That and that and that prowess.
6.translation: That and that and that prowess.

7.word_for_word: उष्णीषाणि शिरोवतं सवस्त्राणि तत्सहितानि शिरांसि ॥७॥ — They wore warm clothes on their heads and their heads with their clothes.
7.translation: They wore warm clothes on their heads and their heads with their clothes.

8.word_for_word: करभाः प्रकोष्ठा ऊरुविशेषणं वा ॥८.९॥ — The handles, the elbows, or the features of the thighs.
8.translation: The handles, the elbows, or the features of the thighs.

9-10.word_for_word: अप्राप्तदारम् एव तं हृतदारमिवातुरम् ॥१०॥ — He was unable to find a wife and was as distressed as if he had been robbed.
9-10.translation: He was unable to find a wife and was as distressed as if he had been robbed.

12.word_for_word: कुहको नर्तयिता तस्येच्छया । — Kuhaka danced at his will.; दुःखेऽपीहमानत्वेन पारवश्यं व्यक्तं दर्शितम् ॥१२॥ — It has been clearly shown that even in suffering he is under the control of the other.
12.translation: Kuhaka danced at his will. It has been clearly shown that even in suffering he is under the control of the other.

13.word_for_word: अत्र चाहम् एव दृष्टान्त इत्य् आह जरासन्धः---शौरेर् इति । — Here I am the illustration, says Jarasandha, the hero.; कृष्णात्सकाशात् । — From the darkness.; एकं संयुगम् । — A compound.; परं केवलमन्तिमं वा जिग्ये जितवानहम् ॥१३॥ — I have conquered the last or only the last I have conquered.
13.translation: Here I am the illustration, says Jarasandha, the hero. From the darkness. A compound. I have conquered the last or only the last I have conquered.

14.word_for_word: दैवमदृष्टं तद्युक्तेन ॥१४॥ — Destiny is not seen by the righteous.
14.translation: Destiny is not seen by the righteous.

15.word_for_word: फल्गुतन्त्रैः स्वल्पसैन्यैः ॥१५॥ — with a small army of small troops.
15.translation: with a small army of small troops.

22-23.word_for_word: गोपालस्य वेदपालकस्येति वास्तवोऽर्थः । — The real meaning of the cowherd is that he is the keeper of the Vedas.; तथा सुदुर्मतेर् इति शोभनाऽनुग्रहवती दुष्टेष्व् अपि मतिर्यस्य तस्येति ॥२२.२३॥ — Similarly, the beautiful and gracious woman whose mind is very wicked is the one whose mind is merciful even to the wicked.
22-23.translation: The real meaning of the cowherd is that he is the keeper of the Vedas. Similarly, the beautiful and gracious woman whose mind is very wicked is the one whose mind is merciful even to the wicked.

24.word_for_word: यदूनां कुलपांसन कुलदूषण वस्तुतस् तु यदूनां कुलस्य पते । — You are the disgrace of the Yadu dynasty and the pollution of the dynasty. In fact, you are the lord of the Yadu dynasty.; हे अंसन स्वयं च रिपुहननचतुर । — O Ansan, you yourself are clever in killing enemies.; अंस समाघाते इत्य् अस्माद्धातोः कर्तरि ल्युट् प्रत्ययो नन्द्यादिविहितः ॥२४॥ — From this the suffix lyut in the doer of the verb 'ansa samaghate' is prescribed by Nandi and others.
24.translation: You are the disgrace of the Yadu dynasty and the pollution of the dynasty. In fact, you are the lord of the Yadu dynasty. O Ansan, you yourself are clever in killing enemies. From this the suffix lyut in the doer of the verb 'ansa samaghate' is prescribed by Nandi and others.

25.word_for_word: ध्वाङ्क्षः काकः स यथा हविर्मुष्णाति तद्वत् । — The crow with the flag is like a crow that burns oblations; वस्तुतस् तु अध्वाङ्क्षवदितिच्छेदः । — In fact, the cut is like a downhill.; सहस्राक्षवद् इत्य् अर्थः । — It means like a thousand eyes.; हे मन्द ! — O slow one!; स्थिरेत्य् अर्थः ॥२५-३३॥ — stable, meaning stable.25-3
25.translation: The crow with the flag is like a crow that burns oblations In fact, the cut is like a downhill. It means like a thousand eyes. O slow one! stable, meaning stable.25-3

34.word_for_word: परित्रासेन विकम्पितान्य् अङ्गानि यस्यास् तया । — She’s the one whose limbs are shaking with fear.; शुचा शोकेन अवशुष्यन् मुखं यस्याः, रुद्धः कण्ठो यस्याः सा च सा च । — She whose mouth was dry with grief and whose throat was choked; तथा कातर्येण वैक्लव्येन विस्रंसिता हेम-मयी माला यस्यास् तया । — Similarly, the woman whose golden necklace was thrown away in fear and anxiety; गृहीतौ पादौ यस्य सः ॥३४॥ — He whose feet are held together.
34.translation: She’s the one whose limbs are shaking with fear. She whose mouth was dry with grief and whose throat was choked Similarly, the woman whose golden necklace was thrown away in fear and anxiety He whose feet are held together.

35.word_for_word: सश्मश्रुकेशं सहितानि स्थाने स्थानेऽवशिष्टानि श्मश्रूणि केशाश् च यथा भवन्ति तथा । — The mustache and hair left in place, including the mustache and hair, are as they are.; तेनैवासिना प्रवपन्मुण्डयन्व्यरूपयद्विरूपमकरोत् ॥३५॥ — With that very sword he shaved his head and disfigured him and disfigured him.
35.translation: The mustache and hair left in place, including the mustache and hair, are as they are. With that very sword he shaved his head and disfigured him and disfigured him.

36.word_for_word: तथा-भूतं हत-प्रायम् इत्य् उत्तर-वाक्ये\ऽप्य् अनुषङ्गः ॥३६-३७॥ — There is also an attachment to the latter statement, that it was almost killed.36-3
36.translation: There is also an attachment to the latter statement, that it was almost killed.36-3

38.word_for_word: रुक्मिणीं सान्त्वयति, मैवास्मानिति ॥३८॥ — He consoles Rukmini, saying, "Not us.

39.word_for_word: पुनः कृष्णमाक्षिपति बन्धुर् इति ॥३९॥ — Again he attracts Krishna, saying, 'My friend.
39.translation: Again he attracts Krishna, saying, 'My friend.

40.word_for_word: पुनर्देवीं प्रत्य् आह---क्षत्रियाणाम् इति । — Again he replied to the goddess, "Of the Kshatriyas.; येन धर्मेण भ्रातापि भ्रातरं हन्यात् । — By the same religion, even a brother can kill his brother.; ततस् तस्माद् धोरतरोऽतिदारुणो धर्मश् च । — Then there was the more dangerous and the more cruel religion.; अतः कोऽस्माकमपराध इति भावः ॥४०॥ — Therefore, who is our fault?
40.translation: Again he replied to the goddess, "Of the Kshatriyas. By the same religion, even a brother can kill his brother. Then there was the more dangerous and the more cruel religion. Therefore, who is our fault?

41.word_for_word: पुनः श्री-कृष्णं प्रत्य् आह---राज्यस्येति । — Again he replied to Sri Krishna, “Of the kingdom.; तथाप्यस्माकमेतदनुचितम् इति भावः ॥४१॥ — Yet this is not appropriate for us, this means.
41.translation: Again he replied to Sri Krishna, “Of the kingdom. Yet this is not appropriate for us, this means.

42.word_for_word: पुनर्देवीं प्रत्य् आह---तवेयम् इति । — Again he replied to the goddess, "This is yours.; सर्वभूतेषु दुर्हृदामहितानां भ्रातॄणामज्ञवद्यद्भद्रं मन्यसे इच्छसि इयं तव विषमा असमीचीना बुद्धिः । — You are ignorant and desire whatever you think is good for your brothers who are hostile to all living beings, and this is your uneven and unfair intelligence.; कुतः । — Where is it from?; यतस् तद् एव सुहृदामभद्रम् इति । — Because that’s what’s wrong with friends.; यद् वा, सर्वभूतेषु दुर्हृदाम् अपि स्वसुहृदां भद्रम् एव दण्डरूपं मुण्डनमभद्रं यन्मन्यसे तवेयं विषमा बुद्धिर् इति । — In other words, you think that shaving your head in the form of punishment is not good for even the worst enemies of all living beings.; अथवा सर्वभूतेषु मध्ये दुर्हृदां शिशुपालादीनामभद्रं सुहृदां भद्रं च यन्मन्यसे तवेयं विषमा बुद्धिः समा न भवति । — Or, perhaps, among all living beings, your unequal intelligence is not equal to what you think is good for those who are unfriendly to you, such as babysitters, and good for your friends.; अज्ञवदज्ञानाम् इव ॥४२॥ — as the ignorant of the ignorant.
42.translation: Again he replied to the goddess, "This is yours. You are ignorant and desire whatever you think is good for your brothers who are hostile to all living beings, and this is your uneven and unfair intelligence. Where is it from? Because that’s what’s wrong with friends. In other words, you think that shaving your head in the form of punishment is not good for even the worst enemies of all living beings. Or, perhaps, among all living beings, your unequal intelligence is not equal to what you think is good for those who are unfriendly to you, such as babysitters, and good for your friends. as the ignorant of the ignorant.

43.word_for_word: कुत इत्यत आह---आत्ममोह इति ॥४३॥ — Where, then, he argues, is self-delusion?
43.translation: Where, then, he argues, is self-delusion?

44.word_for_word: परमार्थम् आह---एक एवेति । — For the ultimate purpose, he argues, there is only one.; परः शुद्धः ज्योतिश् चन्द्रादिर्यथोदकेषु । — The Supreme is pure light, just as the moon and other lights are in water.; नभो यथा घटादिष्व् इति ॥४४॥ — as in the sky in pots and other things.
44.translation: For the ultimate purpose, he argues, there is only one. The Supreme is pure light, just as the moon and other lights are in water. as in the sky in pots and other things.

45.word_for_word: कुतस्तर्हि न चन्द्रादिवदात्मानमेकं शुद्धं प्रतीमस्तत्राह---देह इति । — Why, then, is there no one pure image of the Self, like the moon and others?; द्रव्यमधिभूतम् । — The matter is the supernatural.; प्राणा इन्द्रियाण्यध्यात्मम्, गुणशब्देनाधिदैवं, तत्त्रितयात्मकः । — The life-force is the senses, and the super-god, by the word guna, is composed of the three elements.; देहोपाधिना शुद्धो न प्रतीयत इत्य् अर्थः ॥४५॥ — This means that he is not perceived as pure by the concept of the body.
45.translation: Why, then, is there no one pure image of the Self, like the moon and others? The matter is the supernatural. The life-force is the senses, and the super-god, by the word guna, is composed of the three elements. This means that he is not perceived as pure by the concept of the body.

46.word_for_word:
ननु देहसम्बन्धेनापि संसारे सति शुधत्वं गतम् एव तत्राह---नात्मन इति । — Indeed, even by relation to the body, one has already attained purity in the world.; हे सति ! — O Sati!; अन्येनाधिभूतादिनात्मनः संयोगवियोगौ न स्तः । — There is no union or separation of the self with any other supernatural being.; कुतः । — Where is it from?; असतः असत्त्वादन्यस्येत्य् अर्थः । — This means that there is nothing other than non-existence.; कुतोऽसत्त्वं तत्राह---तद् धेतुत्वाद् इति । — Where is the non-existence?; तस्यान्यस्य भूतेन्द्रियादेः प्रसिद्धेः प्रकाशस्य तद्धेतुत्वादात्महेतुत्वात् । — Because the light of that other being, the senses, etc., is the cause of the fame, it is the cause of the self.; ननु देवैर् अधिष्ठितेभ्य इन्द्रियेभ्यो भूतानां प्रतीतिः प्रसिद्धा । — Indeed, it is well known that the senses possessed by the demigods perceive the living entities.; भूतप्रतीत्या च तत् प्रसिद्धिर् नात्मन इत्यत आह---दृग्रूपाभ्यां यथा रवेः । — And since that fame is not of the self by the perception of beings, he argues that it is as the sun is known by the forms of sight.; यथा प्रकाष्यप्रकाशकत्वेन वर्तमानयोर् अपि चक्षूरूपयोः रवेः सकाशात् प्रसिद्धिर् द्वयोर् अपि तैजसत्वात्तदभेदश् च तथा भूतेन्द्रियादीनां परस्परं सिद्धानाम् अपि चैतन्याधीन एव प्रकाशस् तत् कार्यत्वाच् च तद्-व्यतिरेकेणासत्त्वं चेत्य् अर्थः । — Just as the two forms of the eye, which are present as illuminators, are known from the sun because they are both Taijasa, so the light of the senses and others, which are mutually perfect, is under consciousness because it is its function and is non-existent by its distinction.; तथा च द्वादशे वक्ष्यति, — And so he will say in the twelfth,; > दीपश् चक्षुश् च रूपं च ज्योतिषो न पृथक् भवेत् । — > The lamp, the eye and the form of the light should not be separated.; >
> एवं धीः स्वानि मात्राश् च न स्युर् अन्यतमाद् ऋतात् ॥ — >
> Thus the intellect and its own senses cannot be separated from any other truth.; इति । — It is.; यद् वा, रवेः प्रसिद्धाभ्याम् एव दृग्-रूपाभ्यां परस्परं प्रसिद्धिर् यथा भवति तद्वद् इति ॥४६॥ — That is, as the two well-known forms of sight of the sun are mutually known, so it is said.
46.translation:
Indeed, even by relation to the body, one has already attained purity in the world. O Sati! There is no union or separation of the self with any other supernatural being. Where is it from? This means that there is nothing other than non-existence. Where is the non-existence? Because the light of that other being, the senses, etc., is the cause of the fame, it is the cause of the self. Indeed, it is well known that the senses possessed by the demigods perceive the living entities. And since that fame is not of the self by the perception of beings, he argues that it is as the sun is known by the forms of sight. Just as the two forms of the eye, which are present as illuminators, are known from the sun because they are both Taijasa, so the light of the senses and others, which are mutually perfect, is under consciousness because it is its function and is non-existent by its distinction. And so he will say in the twelfth, > The lamp, the eye and the form of the light should not be separated. >
> Thus the intellect and its own senses cannot be separated from any other truth. It is. That is, as the two well-known forms of sight of the sun are mutually known, so it is said.

47.word_for_word: देहसम्बन्धाभावाद् एव नात्मनो जन्मादयोऽपीति वक्तुं जन्मादीनां देहधर्मत्वम् आह---जन्मादयस्त्व् इति । — To say that the self does not have birth and other things because of the absence of any relationship with the body, he argues that birth and other things are the characteristics of the body.; कथं तर्हि जातोऽहं बालोऽहं वृद्धोऽहम् इत्य् आत्मनि जन्मादिप्रतीतिः । — How, then, is it that the perception of birth and other things in the Self is that I am born, I am a child, I am an old man?; देहजन्मादिनैवेति सदृष्टान्तम् आह---कलानाम् इवेति । — He gives a good example of the birth of the body, as of the arts.; इन्दोः कलानाम् एव जन्मादयो नैवेन्दोर्यथा तद्वत् । — The births and other events of the arts of the moon are not the same as those of the moon.; यथा च कलानाशाद् एव कुहूरमावास्या इन्दुक्षय उच्यते तद्वदस्यात्मनो देहनाशाद् एव मृतिव्यवहार इत्य् अर्थः ॥४७॥ — Just as the Kuhura and the month of Avasya are said to be the decline of the moon by the destruction of the arts, so the behavior of death is destroyed by the destruction of the body of the self, this means.
47.translation: To say that the self does not have birth and other things because of the absence of any relationship with the body, he argues that birth and other things are the characteristics of the body. How, then, is it that the perception of birth and other things in the Self is that I am born, I am a child, I am an old man? He gives a good example of the birth of the body, as of the arts. The births and other events of the arts of the moon are not the same as those of the moon. Just as the Kuhura and the month of Avasya are said to be the decline of the moon by the destruction of the arts, so the behavior of death is destroyed by the destruction of the body of the self, this means.

48.word_for_word: नन्व् आत्मनो देहादिसम्बन्धाभावे कथं भोक्तृभोग्यभोगप्रतीतीत्याशङ्क्य स्वप्नदृष्टान्तेन समर्थयति । — If, however, the self is not connected to the body and other things, how can the enjoyer perceive the enjoyment of the enjoyable?; यथा शयान इति । — For example, lying down.; आत्मानं भोक्तारं विषयान् भोग्यान्फलं भोगमसत्यप्यर्थेऽनुभुङ्क्ते तथा अबुधः सम्सारं प्राप्नोति ॥४८॥ — Thus the ignorant man enjoys himself as the enjoyer of the objects of sense gratification, the fruits of enjoyment, even for the sake of untruth.
48.translation: If, however, the self is not connected to the body and other things, how can the enjoyer perceive the enjoyment of the enjoyable? For example, lying down. Thus the ignorant man enjoys himself as the enjoyer of the objects of sense gratification, the fruits of enjoyment, even for the sake of untruth.

49.word_for_word: आत्मानं शोषयति विमोहयति चेति तथा तम् । — It dries up and confuses itself, and so it does.; निर्हृत्यापाकृत्य ॥४९॥ — Nirhrityapakritya ॥49॥
49.translation: It dries up and confuses itself, and so it does. Nirhrityapakritya ॥49॥

50.word_for_word: समादधे समाहितमकरोत् ॥५०॥ — He took it in his hands and made it concentrated.
50.translation: He took it in his hands and made it concentrated.

51.word_for_word: रुक्मिणस्त्व् एवं श्रुतवतो नाज्ञानं निवृत्तम् इति दर्शयन्न् आह---प्राणावशेष इति ॥५१॥ — Rukmi, however, showing that his ignorance had not ceased when he heard this, said, "There is nothing left of my life.
51.translation: Rukmi, however, showing that his ignorance had not ceased when he heard this, said, "There is nothing left of my life.

52-53.word_for_word: अहत्वा अज्ञात्वादुर्मतिम् इति च सत्योऽर्थः । — And the true meaning is that he killed a fool without knowing it.; अप्रत्यूह्यानावर्त्य । — Apratyuhyanavartya.; अप्रतिबुद्ध्येति तु सत्यम् । — It is true, however, that it is not counter-intuitive.; यवीयसीं स्वसारम् । — the younger sister-in-law.; यत्र विरूपितस् तत्रैवावसत् । — He lived where he was disfigured.; तत्र च भोज-कटं नाम पुरम् अभवत् ॥५२॥ — There was also a town called Bhoja-kata.
52-53.translation: And the true meaning is that he killed a fool without knowing it. Apratyuhyanavartya. It is true, however, that it is not counter-intuitive. the younger sister-in-law. He lived where he was disfigured. There was also a town called Bhoja-kata.

55.word_for_word: वरयोर् वर-वध्वोः पारिबर्हं देयमुपस्करम् ॥५५॥ — The bride and groom should be given the dress and accessories.
55.translation: The bride and groom should be given the dress and accessories.

56.word_for_word: उत्तभितैर् इन्द्रकेतुभि ध्वजविशेषैः । — They were raised by the rainbows and special flags.; उपक्लृप्तानि मङ्गलानि लाजाङ्कुरपुष्पप्रकरादीनि तैः ॥५६॥ — They arranged auspicious things like shame sprouts flowers and other varieties.
56.translation: They were raised by the rainbows and special flags. They arranged auspicious things like shame sprouts flowers and other varieties.

57.word_for_word: आहूताः प्रेष्ठाः भूभुजस्तेषां गजैः परामृष्टा उच्छ्रिता रम्भाश् च पूगाश् च तैर् उपशोभिता यद् वा, तैर् एव गजैः परामृष्टाः संस्पृष्टाः रम्भाश् च पूगाश् च तैर् उपशोभिता ॥५७॥ — The best of the kings were invited They were touched by their elephants They adorned the tall rambhas and beans or whatever else they decorated The rambhas and beans were touched by the same elephants
57.translation: The best of the kings were invited They were touched by their elephants They adorned the tall rambhas and beans or whatever else they decorated The rambhas and beans were touched by the same elephants

58.word_for_word: सम्भ्रमादौत्सुक्यात्परिधावतां बन्धूनां मध्ये मिथः समेत्य मुदं प्रापुः ॥५८.६०॥ — They met each other in the midst of their kinsmen who were running about in excitement and anxiety and rejoiced.
58.translation: They met each other in the midst of their kinsmen who were running about in excitement and anxiety and rejoiced.
